split_policy.primary_axis: tooling/e2e governance contract behavior before fixture directory label, schema JSON, README/package text, compatibility taxonomy label, validator transcript, drift row, invalid-UTF8 row, old-mode label, shim label, fallback label, compatibility label, or migration label
split_policy.positive_rule: extension registry positives are limited to the happy transition/rejection governance fixture owned by the e2e/tooling owner; compatibility fields and compatibility_* wording are taxonomy/provenance labels only and do not define public compatibility support, shims, aliases, fallback, wrappers, or alternate acceptance
split_policy.canonical_rejection_rule: drift scenarios own deterministic rejection for missing validator ordering, schema invariant drift, parity/taxonomy/gating drift, compatibility support overclaims, generated-only rows, report-only rows, migration-only rows, old-mode rows, shim rows, fallback rows, and directory-label-only claims
split_policy.strict_error_rule: invalid UTF-8 scenarios and hard-gate drift promoted as support own fail-closed strict errors and cannot be cited as positive registry capability support
split_policy.provenance_rule: schema JSON, README/package text, validator ids, command anchors, acceptance gate ids, matrix ids, dependency ids, failure taxonomy ids, publication gate ids, validation transcript text, issue/package labels, and compatibility taxonomy labels are fixture provenance unless the e2e/tooling owner claims the scenario boundary
split_policy.retired_surface_rule: old-mode registry support, compatibility support, shim support, fallback support, generated-only registry support, report-only registry support, migration-only registry support, wrapper-only support, runner-only success, workflow-label-only success, and generated/report rows promoted as support are canonical rejection, strict-error, absent-support, or provenance-only evidence
